record.paper_title: Electromagnetic probes in heavy-ion collisions: progress and open questions
record.context_brief: Thermal electromagnetic probes of QGP properties
record.original_question: How can thermal photons and dileptons emitted during the hydrodynamic quark-gluon-plasma stage be used to constrain the plasma space-time profile, chemical and thermal equilibration, temperature-dependent shear and bulk viscosities, possible higher-order transport coefficients, and momentum anisotropy, given that hadronic measurements already strongly constrain low-temperature parts of the hydrodynamic evolution?

evidence.quote: Thermal photons and dileptons are sometimes referred to as “chronometers” and “thermometers” of the plasma, although they face stiff competition from hadrons in that regard.

On the other hand, by focusing on certain bins of momentum and invariant mass and by subtracting certain hadronic decays, it is possible for photons and dileptons to provide information on the earlier stage of the collisions, to which hadrons have limited sensitivity.
Photons and dileptons are more sensitive to the higher temperature regions of the plasma, and can help better constrain the space-time profile of the plasma and its properties

as more measurements, and in particular more precise ones, become available, electromagnetic probes will provide increasingly strong constraints on the chemical and thermal equilibration of the plasma (see Section 4), the temperature dependence of the shear and bulk viscosities, potentially of higher-order transport coefficients [31], and more.
There have also been proposals to use the polarization of photons and dileptons to increase measurements sensitivity to the system’s momentum anisotropy

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a relativistic heavy-ion collision modeled by a hydrodynamic stage of a quark-gluon plasma (QGP) with space-time temperature profile T(x,t), velocity field u^μ(x,t), and dissipative transport coefficients including the temperature-dependent shear viscosity η(T), bulk viscosity ζ(T), and possible second- (or higher-)order transport coefficients. Suppose the plasma may also exhibit incomplete chemical equilibration (parameterized e.g. by a quark fugacity λ_q(T,t) ≤ 1), incomplete thermal equilibration (parameterized e.g. by a non-equilibrium momentum-anisotropy parameter ξ(x,t) characterizing the ratio of longitudinal to transverse momentum scales of partons), and a freeze-out hypersurface Σ_f below which hadronic degrees of freedom govern the dynamics.

Thermal photons are produced from the QGP with a Lorentz-invariant emission rate
  E dN_γ/d^4x d^3k = - (1/(2π)^3) f_B(k·u/T) Im Π^μ_μ^R(k; T, λ_q, ξ, …),
and thermal dileptons of invariant mass M and four-momentum q with rate
  dN_{ℓ^+ℓ^-}/d^4x d^4q = - (α^2/(π^3 M^2)) f_B(q·u/T) Im Π^μ_μ^R(q; T, λ_q, ξ, …),
where Π^μ_μ^R is the retarded electromagnetic current-current correlator of the QGP medium, including viscous corrections to both the distribution functions and the rate.

Assume that hadronic observables (identified-particle spectra, anisotropic flow harmonics v_n, HBT radii, etc.) already strongly constrain the low-temperature portion (T ≲ T_pc, the pseudo-critical temperature) of the hydrodynamic evolution, including η(T) and ζ(T) for T ≲ T_pc.

Problem. Develop a quantitative inference framework that uses measured momentum (k_T) and invariant-mass (M) differential spectra and anisotropic flow coefficients v_n(k_T) and v_n(M) of thermal photons and dileptons—after subtraction of identified hadronic decay contributions and selection of kinematic windows dominated by the QGP stage—to constrain, simultaneously and with quantified uncertainties:
  (i) the QGP space-time temperature profile T(x,t) (in particular the early-time, high-T regions inaccessible to hadrons);
  (ii) the chemical equilibration history λ_q(T,t) and the thermal/momentum-anisotropy history ξ(x,t);
  (iii) the temperature dependence of the shear viscosity η(T)/s(T) and bulk viscosity ζ(T)/s(T) for T > T_pc;
  (iv) at least one second-order transport coefficient (e.g. the shear relaxation time τ_π(T)).

Specifically, determine which combinations of photon and dilepton observables (k_T-bins, M-bins, v_n harmonics) provide independent constraints on each of (i)–(iv), prove or argue under what assumptions these combinations identify the underlying functions uniquely, and quantify the precision with which each quantity can be extracted given current and projected experimental uncertainties.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature treats this as an active, ongoing program. Recent works (e.g. studies of effective QGP temperatures from thermal photon/dilepton production in 2024–2025, and earlier investigations of η/s and ζ/s sensitivity via dilepton radiation) provide partial constraints—dileptons constrain effective temperature and high-T η/s while bulk viscosity affects spectra—but a unified, quantitative inference of T(x,t), chemical/thermal equilibration, η(T), ζ(T), and higher-order transport coefficients from EM probes has not been achieved. The status is open, with partial progress on individual aspects.

status_evidence.title: Effective temperatures of the QGP from thermal photon and dilepton production
status_evidence.snippet: Thermal dileptons are much better probes of the QGP temperature... allowing for a more precise constraint of the QGP temperature during different stages of the evolution.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2024) work shows dileptons can constrain effective QGP temperature, partial progress on (i).

status_evidence.title: Investigating the temperature dependence of the specific shear viscosity of QCD matter with dilepton radiation, Phys. Rev. C 98, 014902
status_evidence.snippet: The elliptic flow of thermal dileptons can resolve the magnitude of η/s at high temperatures... discriminating between different specific functional forms will likely not be possible at RHIC.
status_evidence.claim: Partial constraint on η(T)/s only; full functional form not yet extractable.

status_evidence.title: Bulk viscous effects on flow and dilepton radiation in a hybrid approach
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates how bulk viscosity affects dilepton spectra and flow.
status_evidence.claim: Bulk viscosity ζ(T) inference from dileptons is being studied but not fully resolved.
